title: Why does cold water taste sweet on a hot day?

segments.text: Why does ice cold water taste almost sweet on a hot day? There's no sugar in it. So what's going on?
Here's the twist. Cold actually makes things taste less sweet.
Your sweet sensor is a tiny channel called {TRPM5.|T R P M five.} It fires harder when it's warm, and slows down when it's cold. That's why melted ice cream tastes way too sweet.

So the sweetness is in your brain. In {1971,|nineteen seventy one,} a scientist named Michel Cabanac showed that the same feeling can be lovely or awful, depending on what your body needs. Overheated? Cold feels amazing.
Here's the wild part. Water takes tens of minutes to reach your blood. But your brain doesn't wait. Sensors in your mouth switch off your thirst neurons almost instantly.
In mice, cold water did it with fewer sips.
So that sweet sip isn't sugar. It's your brain saying thank you.
